body: In this easy-level conversation, two presenters talk about grumpy days - those mornings when everything feels annoying before you even leave the house.
在这期简易对话里，两位主持人聊了「脾气差的日子」——门都还没出，什么事都让你烦。
They explain that being grumpy is usually short and small. You are not angry, just tired, hungry or woken up too early, so you answer people in short sentences.
他们说「grumpy」通常是短暂的小情绪：你不是真生气，只是累了、饿了或者被叫早了，所以说话又短又没耐心。
Their advice is simple: name the feeling, take a break, eat something, and tell the people around you that it is not their fault.
他们给的办法很简单：先说出这个情绪，歇一会儿，吃点东西，再告诉身边人「不是你的问题」。
tips: 对某人没耐心地吼一句

body: The presenters talk about food that burns your mouth, and why some people love that feeling while others avoid it completely.
主持人聊到那些辣得嘴巴发烫的菜，以及为什么有人爱这种感觉、有人躲得远远的。
One of them says spicy food makes you sweat and drink a lot of water, but it also makes simple dishes much more interesting.
其中一位说，辣的东西会让你出汗、猛喝水，但也能把很普通的菜变得有意思。
They also share a useful tip: milk or yoghurt helps more than water when your mouth is on fire.
他们还给了个实用小知识：嘴里像着火的时候，牛奶或酸奶比白水管用。
tips: 我的嘴像着火了（形容太辣）

body: This conversation looks at what it is really like to live in a big city, with both the good side and the bad side.
这期对话聊的是住在大城市到底什么感觉，好的一面和难受的一面都说了。
The good side: buses and trains everywhere, jobs, restaurants, and something to do at any hour. The bad side: noise, crowds and high rent.
好处是：公交地铁到处都有，工作多、餐厅多，任何时间都有事可做。坏处是：吵、人多、房租贵。
They agree that many people move to a city for work when they are young, and later want somewhere quieter and cheaper.
他们都同意：很多人年轻时为了工作去大城市，后来又想找个更安静、更便宜的地方。

articles.zh: 「你的人生故事」——没人问就别全说
body: This short programme teaches the phrase "I didn't ask for your life story", used when someone answers a simple question with far too much detail.
这期短节目教的是「I didn't ask for your life story」，用在别人回答一个小问题却讲了一大堆的时候。
It is usually said in a joking way between friends. Said to a stranger or a boss, it sounds rude.
这句话通常是朋友之间开玩笑说的；对陌生人或上司说，就显得很不客气了。
A softer version is "long story short", which you can use yourself before giving a short answer.
更客气的说法是自己先讲「long story short」（长话短说），然后给个简短回答。
tips: 长篇大论的经历、来龙去脉

body: The phrase "keep yourself to yourself" describes someone who stays private and does not mix much with neighbours or workmates.
「keep yourself to yourself」用来说一个人比较私密、不太跟邻居或同事打交道。
It is not an insult. Sometimes it is a choice: you are busy, you are tired, or you simply enjoy your own company.
这不是骂人的话。有时候这就是一种选择：你忙、你累，或者你就是喜欢独处。
But the programme reminds us that too much of it can feel lonely, so a short chat with a neighbour still helps.
但节目也提醒：过头了会孤单，所以跟邻居聊两句还是有好处的。
tips: 不爱与人来往、比较私密
